original_idea: Uma ferramenta de linha de comando simples que recebe um nome de arquivo e cria uma cópia com timestamp antes de alterações manuais, sem banco de dados, interface gráfica ou sincronização.
current_idea: A command-line utility that takes a file path as input and creates a duplicate of the file with a timestamp appended to its name, intended to be run manually before editing the original file, and operates without any database, graphical interface, or synchronization components.
human_intent: Create a simple command-line utility that automatically generates a timestamped backup copy of a specified file prior to manual modification.
problem_statement: Users need a quick way to preserve the current state of a file before making manual edits, without relying on databases, GUIs, or synchronization services.
assumptions: User has read/write permissions for the target file
Tool runs on a local machine
User will invoke the tool before editing
Timestamp format is acceptable to the filesystem
Operating system supports standard file operations
ambiguities: Whether the backup is stored in the same directory or a separate backup directory
How to handle existing backup files with same timestamp
Support for multiple files or directories
strengths: No need for databases or GUI

critical_issues.issue: Reliance on user to run the tool before editing can be forgotten, leading to loss of changes
critical_issues.why_it_matters: The core value of preserving file state is nullified if the backup is not created, making the tool ineffective

critical_issues.issue: Timestamp format may include characters illegal on some filesystems (e.g., ':' on Windows)
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Backup files could fail to be created or be inaccessible, breaking the utility

critical_issues.issue: Copy operation is not atomic; interruption can leave a corrupted backup
critical_issues.why_it_matters: User may rely on a backup that is incomplete, causing data loss when editing

fragile_assumptions: User has read/write permissions for the target file
Timestamp format is acceptable to the filesystem
User will invoke the tool before editing
Operating system supports standard file operations
contradictions: The claim of a "quick" manual step conflicts with the need for disciplined user action, which can be error‑prone
failure_modes: Insufficient disk space causing incomplete backup
Partial file created if process is killed

alternatives.mechanism: Wrap the edit command in a shell function that first creates an atomic backup using a safe timestamp format and then launches the editor
addresses_issues: User forgets to run tool (the wrapper is invoked automatically when editing)
Timestamp format sanitized to avoid illegal characters
Backup performed via copy‑then‑rename to make it atomic
tradeoffs: Requires users to adopt the wrapper or alias
Adds a small overhead before opening the editor
Only works when the wrapper is used, not for external editors
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Uses a shell wrapper to embed backup creation into the edit workflow, eliminating manual step.

alternatives.mechanism: Deploy a lightweight file‑system watcher (e.g., inotify on Linux, FSEvents on macOS, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows) that watches the target file and automatically creates a timestamped backup whenever the file is opened for write
addresses_issues: Eliminates reliance on user to remember to run the tool
Generates timestamp using ISO‑8601 without ':' to stay legal
Creates backup by copying to a temp file then renaming, ensuring atomicity
tradeoffs: Requires a background process to stay running
May generate backups for unintended writes (e.g., autosave)
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Introduces an always‑on watcher that autonomously backs up on write events.

alternatives.mechanism: Integrate the backup step into the file‑save operation via a custom editor plugin (e.g., a Vim/VSCode extension) that, on save, copies the file to a backup directory with a sanitized timestamp and uses atomic rename
addresses_issues: User cannot forget because backup is tied to save action
Timestamp format can be controlled to avoid illegal characters
Atomic rename ensures backup is not left corrupted
tradeoffs: Requires installing and configuring the plugin for each editor
Limited to editors that support extensions
Adds slight delay on each save
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Leverages editor extensibility to embed backup creation directly into the save lifecycle.

core_mechanism: The tool receives a file name as an argument and creates a copy of that file with a timestamp added to the filename.
